newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO detains award-winning Palestinian journalist.
newsitem.headline: PLO detains award-winning Palestinian journalist.

text.p: Palestinian journalist Daoud Kuttab, winner of the International Press Freedom Award, has been detained and held without charge by the Palestinian Authority, Kuttab's brother said on Wednesday.
"Captain Faris from the criminal police summoned Daoud from his home last night about 11 p.m. and when he went there they kept him," his brother Jonathan Kuttab told Reuters.
Kuttab lives in East Jerusalem and was detained in the West Bank self-rule enclave of Ramallah. Palestinian police were not immediately available to comment.

The brother said the detention was apparently related to a dispute between Kuttab, who has a private contract to carry live broadcasts of Palestinian Legislative Council sessions, and Palestinian state-run television.

"He has been running into problems with jamming of their broadcast by the Palestinian authorities, by Palestinian television, in order to block council sessions critical of the Palestinian Authority," Jonathan Kuttab said.
"There are some people within the executive branch who do not feel comfortable with that level of openness or criticism."
The brother said Kuttab was being well-treated in jail.
Kuttab is dean of the Modern Communications Centre at al-Quds University.

He was awarded the International Press Freedom Award last year by the New York based Committee to Protect Journalists for his work challenging censorship practices of both Israeli and Palestinian authorities.
